findings.title: ElementDefinition no longer accepts previously valid BPMN type strings
findings.why_it_matters: The exported ElementDefinition.type contract changed from string to a small BpmnElementType union. This is a source-breaking change for TypeScript consumers: previously valid calls for standard BPMN types outside the engine's current mutation subset (for example bpmn:Transaction or bpmn:EventSubProcess) now fail to compile, including callers of the separately exported ElementFactory that still forwards any supplied type to bpmn-js. There is no versioned replacement type or migration boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the externally accepted type as string (or introduce a wider documented BpmnTypeInput) and validate/narrow inside SimpleBpmnEngine; alternatively make this an explicit major-version contract change and provide a migration path. Add a compile-time public API fixture showing the intended support or rejection behavior for an existing standard BPMN type outside the editable union.
evidence: ElementDefinition.type was string in HEAD and is now BpmnElementType at src/types/index.ts:52-54; BpmnElementType is limited to the listed flow-node/artifact types plus Participant (src/types/index.ts:11-50).

ElementFactory.createElement, createAndConnect, and appendShape remain public methods accepting ElementDefinition and pass definition.type directly to bpmn-js (src/core/ElementFactory.ts:17-35, 64-85, and 91-127).
No compatibility overload, deprecated legacy input type, or package major-version change accompanies the narrowing.

findings.title: ProcessContext became incompatible with existing constructed contexts
findings.why_it_matters: ProcessContext is exported and its new document field is required, while elements and connections narrowed from Map<string, any> to typed maps. Consumers that construct a context using the former public shape now fail type-checking, and consumers that retain broader element maps cannot assign them. This is a breaking request/response-model change without an additive legacy shape or migration guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the typed document model as a new versioned context shape, or make document optional during a deprecation transition and normalize legacy contexts at the API boundary. Publish a constructor/factory as the supported creation contract and add a compile-time compatibility fixture for external ProcessContext consumers.
evidence: HEAD defined ProcessContext with id, name, type, Map<string, any> elements/connections, and optional xml only; the current exported interface adds required document and typed map values (src/types/index.ts:150-160).
The change exposes ProcessContext through public engine methods such as createProcess, importXml, loadDiagram, and getProcess (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:60, 353, 381, and 409).

Current construction is internalized through createProcessContext (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:117-131), but the exported interface itself provides neither a compatibility union nor a migration factory requirement.

findings.title: The promised lossless import/export contract drops unindexed sequence flows
findings.why_it_matters: The import/export API now promises preservation of the complete imported moddle graph while exposing only a typed mutation subset. A SequenceFlow connected to a valid but unindexed BPMN node is deliberately omitted from the editable map, then the retained serializer treats the omission as a delete. An open/export operation therefore returns XML with unrelated semantic and DI objects missing, violating the behavioral contract even when the caller requests no mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Represent intentional API deletions independently from parse-time omissions (for example through explicit deletion IDs), and detach only explicit deletions. Add a black-box import/export contract test with an unindexed valid BPMN endpoint, its SequenceFlow, and BPMNEdge.
evidence: assertImportedConnections removes a SequenceFlow from document.connections if either endpoint is outside the typed index and explicitly says it should remain in sourceXml (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:1091-1097).
serializeRetained detaches every parsed bpmn:SequenceFlow absent from document.connections (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:426-428).

Executable black-box reproduction: importing Transaction T -> Task A with SequenceFlow F and BPMNEdge F_di, then exporting without edits, produced indexed:[] and transaction:true, flow:false, edge:false from bpmn-moddle.

residual_risks: The package export currently targets the MCP server entrypoint, but these source-level exported interfaces are still part of the generated declaration surface for direct module consumers; an explicit supported-consumer policy is not documented.
The canonical rich-fixture tests pass for the represented BPMN subset, but that does not establish a compatibility promise for standard constructs outside BpmnElementType.
testing_gaps: Add TypeScript public-contract fixtures for legacy ElementDefinition and ProcessContext construction, with an explicit expected migration policy.
Add black-box no-op and targeted-edit import/export tests covering an unindexed standard BPMN node connected by a SequenceFlow and its BPMN DI edge.
Document and test whether direct package consumers may import these generated types/modules, or provide a stable public barrel with versioned types.
